entries.reason: money() is deliberately unsupported: SharpMUSH does not track pennies (function answers '#-1 NOT SUPPORTED').
PennMUSH reports its attribute-chunk allocator; SharpMUSH stores attributes in its database and has no allocator to report.
entries.profile: PennMUSH's file and allocator housekeeping answers `NOT SUPPORTED`

entries.reason: PennMUSH checks the password and would wipe its own log file; SharpMUSH's logs go to configured sinks the game does not own, so @logwipe refuses before any password check.
entries.profile: PennMUSH's file and allocator housekeeping answers `NOT SUPPORTED`

entries.reason: PennMUSH gives a STICKY room's drop-to move to SYSEVENT (#-1 as the handler sees it); SharpMUSH has no SYSEVENT object and passes on the player whose leaving caused the move.
entries.profile: A drop-to move's event names who caused it

entries.reason: PennMUSH refuses a MAILFILTER folder name the player has not used yet; SharpMUSH creates the folder and files the message.
entries.profile: Folders are named freely and created on delivery

entries.reason: PennMUSH reads an empty MAILFORWARDLIST as a list naming nobody and drops the mail; SharpMUSH treats it as no list and delivers normally.

PennMUSH applied @find's restrict_command line once, so the @command/restrict after it stands; SharpMUSH applies command_restrictions again when it changes, which puts @find back to the line's wizard restriction.

The reference PennMUSH runs with the shipped restrict.cnf, whose `restrict_command @destroy noplayer " Use @recycle instead` (game/restrictcnf.dst:86) refuses a player's @destroy before it runs; SharpMUSH ships command_restrictions empty, so the command destroys the thing. Not pinned with `sharp`: the refusal is all of PennMUSH's side, and SharpMUSH's side is the unparse of the destroyed object, whose flag letters are still GRA-141 (#1404).
entries.profile: A new game restricts no commands

entries.reason: Clearing an attribute that is not there is AE_NOTFOUND. PennMUSH notifies 'No such attribute to reset.' and returns nothing; SharpMUSH's attrib_set() returns the reason instead, as it does for its other failures.

Clearing looks the name up exactly (find_atr_in_list), so clearing DESC while DESCRIBE is set is AE_NOTFOUND and DESCRIBE stays. PennMUSH notifies 'No such attribute to reset.'; SharpMUSH's attrib_set() returns the reason instead.
entries.sharp:
Wiz/DESCRIBE - Set.
Wiz/DESCRIBE - Cleared.
#-1 NO SUCH ATTRIBUTE|d
entries.penn:
Wiz/DESCRIBE - Set.
No such attribute to reset.
Wiz/DESCRIBE - Cleared.
|d

entries.reason: PennMUSH's attrib_set() fails silently on an object the caller does not control, whether or not the attribute exists, and mailstats() notifies 'The post office protects privacy!' and returns nothing; SharpMUSH returns the reason from each, and the same refusal for a missing attribute, so existence is not revealed.
entries.sharp: #-1 NO PERMISSION TO SET ATTRIBUTE|#-1 PERMISSION DENIED|#-1 NO PERMISSION TO SET ATTRIBUTE

entries.reason: decompose() writes colour inside colour as nested ansi() calls; PennMUSH writes flat calls with combined codes. Both evaluate to the same string.
decompose() writes a tag as tagwrap(), the call that makes it here; PennMUSH writes tag()/endtag(), which SharpMUSH answers with 'use tagwrap'.
entries.profile: `decompose()` writes tags and links as the calls that make them

entries.reason: %> is the output of the last command in the same queue entry, empty on a typed line; PennMUSH has no %> substitution and evaluates it to >.
%| is what the command before a ;| showed, empty everywhere else (TinyMUX piping); PennMUSH has no %| substitution and evaluates it to |.
SharpMUSH draws the folder report as a titled panel (a table of folders, then the current folder under a divider); PennMUSH prints one MAIL: line per folder.
entries.profile: Mail listings are drawn as panels
